title: Costmap Layers: What Is Known to Be There, What Was Just Seen, and What Is Too Close to It, Kept Apart so That Each Can Be Cleared Without Losing the Others

questions.question: What question is a costmap built to answer?
options: May the centre of the vehicle be here?
questions.explanation: The vehicle's size is folded into the map by inflation.

questions.question: A wall of 4 m at 0.05 m resolution was how many lethal cells?
At 0.50 m from a post, with an inscribed radius of 0.25 m and a scale of 3, the cost was:
The layer that only marks left how many ghost cells when the obstacle went?
Why can the planner treat the vehicle as a point after inflation?
options: The inscribed radius already keeps the centre far enough from every obstacle
questions.explanation: The footprint is in the map.

questions.question: Why was a gap of 0.40 m closed for a vehicle 0.50 m wide?
options: The inflation of both posts covers it, so no cell across it is below 253
questions.explanation: The map knows the vehicle's width.
